beats.narration_text: Reel-updater has three parts. A drift detector that reads every beat_sheet and flags old mascot outro patterns, orphan audio, and out-of-sync narration. A stripper that restores pristine narration and cleans the outro work files. And an appender — the next phase — that adds the two new Remotion outro beats and generates only their audio.

props.sparkLine: Strip the old. Append the new. Never re-spend the body.

beats.narration_text: The pipeline: detect drift — old outro, orphan audio, missing audio. Plan the strip. Strip the non-Remotion outro: delete the mascot media, restore the pristine narration, reset actual-duration-s, clean work files. Delete orphan audio. Then — once the Remotion compositions exist — append the two new outro beats and generate only their audio. compile produces the fresh cut.

props.title: migration audit — free drift scan
props.code:
import glob, json
# find reels with saved pristine outros
orig = glob.glob(
  'books/*/youtube/*/clips/_work/outro-orig-*.mp3'
)
reels = set(f.split('/clips/')[0] for f in orig)
print(f'migrated: {len(reels)} reels')
# scan all beat_sheets for remaining drift
all_bs = glob.glob(
  'books/*/youtube/*/beat_sheet.json'
)
drift = 0
for r in all_bs:
    bs = json.load(open(r))
    for b in bs.get('beats', []):
        if b.get('shot',{}).get('source')=='outro':
            drift += 1; break
print(f'drift: {drift} | total: {len(all_bs)}')
# migrated: 83 reels
# drift: 0 | total: 2761
props.sparkLine: 83 migrated. 0 drift. 2761 scanned. Fleet is clean.

beats.narration_text: Law one: dry-run by default. You never run update and accidentally delete files. The script reads every beat_sheet, detects drift, prints the plan, and writes UPDATE dot md. Nothing changes until you pass dash dash apply. As the SKILL.md says — dry-run by default. It prints the plan and writes UPDATE.md; it changes nothing.

props.heading: Dry-run by default.
props.body: Read every beat_sheet. Detect drift. Print the plan. Write UPDATE.md. Nothing changes until --apply. Safe to run at any time.
props.quote: Dry-run by default. It prints the plan and writes UPDATE.md; it changes nothing.
props.sparkLine: Plan first. Apply only when you've reviewed.

beats.narration_text: Law two: credit discipline. The strip itself costs nothing — it restores the pristine narration that was saved before the mascot outro was generated. The body's audio is never re-generated. The only audio spend is for the two new outro beats, and that runs with dash dash only, billing exactly those two beats. As the SKILL says: credit discipline — the strip spends nothing. Only the new outro beats ever get new audio.

props.heading: Credit discipline.
props.body: Strip: restore outro-orig narration — free. Body audio: never re-generated. Only the two new outro beats bill, via generate_audio.py --only.
props.quote: Credit discipline: the strip spends nothing. Only the new outro beats ever get new audio, via generate_audio.py --only
props.sparkLine: Strip for free. Pay only for what's new.

beats.narration_text: Law three: idempotent. Run it once, run it a hundred times — same result. A reel with no mascot outro and no orphans is reported clean and skipped. Re-running is safe. This is what makes update-all safe to run across 2761 reels: the ones already done are just reported clean. No double-deletion, no double-billing.

props.body: Already migrated → reported clean, skipped. Double-running is safe. 83 reels already done; re-running hits 0 drift.

props.sparkLine: Run it as many times as you need. Clean is clean.

beats.narration_text: Verdict: reel-updater migrates the fleet without re-spending audio credits. Dry-run by default means the plan is always reviewed before files change. Credit discipline means only the new beats bill. And idempotency means the migration can run across thousands of reels without side effects. The fleet is clean.
